text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today even as crude oil prices remain elevated, caught between competing forces. Geopolitical tensions—Saudi pipeline shutdowns, Houthi advances threatening the Red Sea shipping lane, and escalating U.S. pressure on Iran—have pushed global crude to $109.51 a barrel, yet U.S. crude slipped below $100 today after a multiday rally. The stock's modest decline suggests the market is taking a cautious view on oil supply disruption news, or profit-taking after the stock gained 5.67% over two weeks.

The gap between U.S. crude ($97.26) and global crude ($109.51) reflects real supply concerns abroad, but U.S.-focused energy companies like ConocoPhillips benefit more from domestic pricing; the pullback in WTI crude today appears to be weighing more than the geopolitical premium baked into Brent.
